correctness.rationale: All positive geodesics can be chosen simple and a complete junction-to-junction traversal of any longer edge is replaced by shorter a; endpoints on shortest edge cannot yield full traversal. For two points on one longer edge length ell_i, the transit event is two triangles of total product area d_i^2/4, with barycentric triangle coordinates Dirichlet(1,1,1). For distinct longer edges i,j, comparing all four candidate simple path lengths gives the two disjoint corner rectangles, each area d_i d_j/4 per ordered pair, yielding d_i d_j per unordered pair over the two point orders and independently uniform conditional rectangle coordinates. Normalizing by L^2 proves the probability and mixture law. For fixed sum S= L-ma>0, Cauchy sum d_i^2 >=S^2/(m-1), positivity sum d_i^2 <S^2 yield the exact strict lower bound and attained equal-edges upper bound, plus global unattained supremum. Independently performed midpoint-grid path-minimum integration over 3 distinct 3–5 edge configurations, with agreement to ~0.002, and inspected source verify.py. Grid checks are not proof for arbitrary real lengths; domain partitions are.

final_claim: For a two-vertex m>=3 compact parallel-edge metric graph with shortest edge a and every other length ell_i>a, arclength-uniform random point-pair geodesic traverses the entire shortest edge with probability (sum d_i^2/4 + sum_{i<j}d_i d_j)/L^2; no longer edge is completely traversed, and exact Dirichlet/uniform conditional laws and sharp fixed-L,a,m bounds hold.
limitations: Only m>=3 with strict unique shortest edge, positive real lengths and arclength-uniform independent points; no general network traffic claims.
Finite grid Monte Carlo corroboration cannot establish the exact all-real-length theorem.
